summary: A deliberate fault injection (CHG-1c22e75c) SIGTERM'd redis2 - one of three Redis Cluster masters holding 5462 slots - and because the cluster runs with zero replicas, no failover was possible, leaving the slot range uncovered and driving the entire cluster into CLUSTERDOWN, which halted both the enricher and the ingest server.
reasoning: Confirmed via four independent sources agreeing within ~20 seconds: the redis2 container log (SIGTERM at 20:10:51, clean shutdown, no crash/OOM), the Prometheus cluster metrics (redis_cluster_state 1->0, redis_cluster_slots_fail=5462, redis_connected_slaves=0), the application logs (CLUSTERDOWN from go-server, dial failures to .101 from go-enricher), and the change ledger (inject CHG-1c22e75c at 20:10:50Z, no restore). Also flagged two secondary findings ruled out as causal: a 5MB maxmemory/allkeys-lru setting already evicting ~2 keys/sec before the incident (pre-existing, unrelated), and the zero-replica topology as the structural reason any single master loss takes down the whole cluster rather than degrading a third of it.
